exampleAnswers.title: Describing Properties of the Tangent Function

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\tan{x}?$ Assume that $n$ represents any integer.

  1. The function has asymptotes at $x= \pi n.$
  2. $\tan\left(x - \dfrac \pi 4 \right) = \tan\left(x+\dfrac{3\pi}{4} \right).$
  3. The function is strictly increasing on the interval $\left( -\dfrac{3\pi}{2},-\dfrac{\pi}{2} \right).$
question.explanation:
Let's recall the graph of $y=\tan x.$

Let's examine each statement.

  • Statement I is false. The function $y=\tan{x}$ has asymptotes at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \pi n.$

  • Statement II is true. The function $y=\tan{x}$ has period $\pi.$ So, $\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{4}+ \pi \right)=\tan\left(x+\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right).$

  • Statement III is true. The function is strictly increasing on each interval $\left( -\dfrac{\pi}{2}+n\pi ,\dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi \right).$ If we take $n=-1$ we get the interval $\left( -\dfrac{3\pi}{2},-\dfrac{\pi}{2} \right).$

example.title: Describing Properties of the Tangent Function

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\tan{x}?$ Assume that $n$ represents any integer.

  1. The vertical asymptotes of the function are $x =2n\pi$
  2. Its graph passes through the point $(0,0)$
  3. $\tan\left(x - \dfrac{\pi}6 \right) = \tan\left(x+\dfrac{5\pi}6 \right)$
question.explanation:
Let's recall the graph of $y=\tan x.$

Let's examine each statement.

  • Statement I is false. The function has an asymptote at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and the period is $\pi.$ Therefore, the asymptotes occur at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi.$

  • Statement II is true. Indeed, the graph of the function passes through the point $(0,0).$

  • Statement III is true. The function $y=\tan{x}$ has period $\pi.$ So, $\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\tan\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{6}+ \pi \right)=\tan\left(x+\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right).$

So, the correct answer is "II and III only".

exampleAnswers.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Tangent Function

question.text: If $\tan x = \dfrac{5}{4},$ for some value of $x,$ find the value of $24\tan(x - 11\pi)-3.$
question.explanation:
The period of $y = \tan x$ is $\pi.$ Therefore, for any integer $n,$ we have

\[ \tan{x} = \tan(x+n\pi). \]

Substituting $n=-11$ into the above gives \begin{align*} \tan{x} = \tan(x+(-11)\cdot\pi) = \tan(x-11\pi). \end{align*}

Since $\tan{x} = \dfrac{5}{4},$ we get that $\tan(x - 11\pi) = \dfrac{5}{4}.$ Therefore \[ 24\tan(x - 11\pi) - 3 = 24\left( \dfrac{5}{4} \right) - 3 = 30-3 = 27. \]

example.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Tangent Function

question.text: If $\tan x = 10,$ for some value of $x,$ find the value of $\dfrac{1}{2}\tan(x -3\pi).$
question.explanation:
The period of $y = \tan x$ is $\pi.$ Therefore, for any integer $n,$ we have \[ \tan{x} = \tan(x + n\pi). \]

Substituting $n=-3$ into the above gives \begin{align*} \tan{x} = \tan(x + (-3)\cdot\pi) = \tan(x - 3\pi). \end{align*}

Since $\tan{x} = 10,$ we get that $\tan(x - 3\pi) = 10.$ Therefore \[ \dfrac{1}{2}\tan(x - 3\pi) = \dfrac{1}{2}(10) = 5. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Utilizing the Oddness Property of the Tangent Function

question.explanation:
First, let's recall the graph of $y=\tan{x}.$

From the graph, we note the following:

  • The period of $\tan{x}$ is $\pi.$

  • Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. This means that $\tan{x}$ is an odd function, and we have \[ \tan(-x) = -\tan{x}. \]

Let's now evaluate our expression:

  • Firstly, using the periodicity of $\tan{x},$ we have \begin{align} \tan(-a+9\pi) &= \tan(-a + \pi \cdot 9) \\[5pt] &= \tan(-a). \end{align}

  • Secondly, using the oddness of $\tan{x},$ we have \begin{align} \tan(-a) &= -\tan{a} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac52. \end{align}

Therefore, $\tan (-a+12\pi)=-\dfrac{5}{2}.$

example.title: Utilizing the Oddness Property of the Tangent Function

question.explanation:
First, let's recall the graph of $y=\tan{x}.$

From the graph, we note the following:

  • The period of $\tan{x}$ is $\pi.$

  • Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. This means that $\tan{x}$ is an odd function, and we have \[ \tan(-x) = -\tan{x}. \]

Let's now evaluate our expression:

  • Firstly, using the periodicity of $\tan{x},$ we have \begin{align} \tan(-x-5\pi) &= \tan(-x - \pi \cdot 5) \\[5pt] &= \tan(-x). \end{align}

  • Secondly, using the oddness of $\tan{x},$ we have \begin{align} \tan(-x) &= -\tan{x} \\[5pt] &= -4. \end{align}

Therefore, $\tan (-x-5\pi)=-4.$
